title: Tutorial: k-means clustering
text: naive test applies Hotelling’s T2T^2 test estimated clusters chosen advance. compute every pair clusters, next selective test. tests reject every null hypothesis , three groups really differ. difference tests appears groups .
code: naive_pval <- function(X, cl, k1, k2) {   n1 <- sum(cl == k1); n2 <- sum(cl == k2); p <- ncol(X); r <- n1 + n2   F_stat <- (r - p - 1) / ((r - 2) * p) * hotelling_T2(X, cl, k1, k2)   pf(F_stat, p, r - p - 1, lower.tail = FALSE) }  pairs <- rbind(c(1, 2), c(1, 3), c(2, 3)) results <- t(apply(pairs, 1, function(k) {   set.seed(1)   # the same initial centers, so the same clustering, for every pair   sel <- selective_hotelling_test(X, k[1], k[2], K = 3, M = 1000)   c(k1 = k[1], k2 = k[2], naive = naive_pval(X, sel$cluster, k[1], k[2]),     selective = sel$pval) })) signif(results, 3) #>      k1 k2    naive selective #> [1,]  1  2 4.64e-55   0.00497 #> [2,]  1  3 8.41e-60   0.00596 #> [3,]  2  3 1.24e-84   0.00397

text: see coincidence, repeat null experiment 300300 times n=60n = 60 plot quantiles pp-values uniform distribution. skip rare data sets tested cluster fewer three observations, Hotelling’s T2T^2 defined. test controls Type error pp-values diagonal.  level 0.050.05, naive test rejects 100% true null hypotheses selective test 7.4%. 300300 data sets, second number Monte Carlo standard error 1.31.3 percentage points; run 2,0002{,}000 data sets, selective test rejected 4.7%4.7\%.
code: set.seed(2024) sim <- t(replicate(300, {   Xs <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 2), ncol = 2) %*% chol(Sigma)   rs <- tryCatch(selective_hotelling_test(Xs, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, M = 200),                  error = function(e) NULL)   # skip the rare data sets with a tiny cluster   if (is.null(rs)) c(naive = NA, selective = NA)   else c(naive = naive_pval(Xs, rs$cluster, 1, 2), selective = rs$pval) })) sim <- sim[complete.cases(sim), ] nrow(sim) #> [1] 299 u <- ppoints(nrow(sim)) plot(u, sort(sim[, "naive"]), pch = 19, col = "black", xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),      xlab = "Uniform(0, 1) quantiles", ylab = "p-value quantiles") points(u, sort(sim[, "selective"]), pch = 19, col = "steelblue") abline(0, 1, lty = 2) legend("topleft", c("naive", "selective"), col = c("black", "steelblue"), pch = 19,        bty = "n") colMeans(sim <= 0.05) #>     naive selective  #> 1.0000000 0.0735786

title: Algorithm-agnostic Besag-Clifford selective Hotelling test (arbitrary clustering) — selective_hotelling_bc
text: Monte Carlo selective test equality means discovered cluster pair (k1, k2), valid clustering X arbitrary black-box clustering routine cl_fun, treating covariance \(\Sigma\) unknown. package's entry point selective inference clustering algorithm (hierarchical clustering, fixed-init k-means, spectral clustering, ...), contrast selective_hotelling_test(), hard-wired k-means. construction exactly Besag Clifford (1991), transported Stiefel manifold. null observed polar factor \(Q_{obs}\) uniform feasible region \(E = \{Q \St(r-1, p) : cl\_fun(X(Q))\ \mathrm{preserves}\ (k_1,k_2)\}\) regardless \(\Sigma\). build Metropolis kernel \(K\) \(E\) using symmetric Cayley proposal \(Q' = U Q\) (\(U\) random Cayley rotation step eps) accepted iff \(Q' \E\); flat target restricted \(E\) acceptance ratio indicator \(1\{Q' \E\}\), \(K\) (\(K^L\)) reversible w.r.t. \(\mathrm{Uniform}(E)\). plant \(Q_{obs}\) uniform random index \(J \\{0,\dots,M\}\) run \(K^L\) forward \(J \M\) backward \(J \0\). seed stationary \(K^L\) reversible, rank contrast statistic \(u(Q) = \|Q'v\|^2\) (strictly monotone pair's two-sample Hotelling \(T^2\)) \(Q_{obs}\) among \(M+1\) path marks exactly \(\mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dots,M+1\}\). Hence randomized upper-tail rank p-value exactly \(\mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)\) \(H_0\). Validity holds reversible kernel, step eps, path length M, clustering cl_fun. Mixing (governed eps, L, acceptance rate) buys power , never validity.

title: Algorithm-agnostic Besag-Clifford selective Hotelling test (arbitrary clustering) — selective_hotelling_bc
text: X numeric \(n \times p\) data matrix observations rows. cl_fun black-box clustering routine: function function(Xmat) -> integer label vector (list carrying $cluster, e.g. result stats::kmeans()). must pure function data argument (data-independent randomness allowed, e.g. fixed initialization deterministic algorithm hierarchical clustering). called X obtain observed clustering many times reconstructed data \(X(Q)\) sampling. k1, k2 two tested cluster labels, labelling cl_fun(X). cluster must least three members Hotelling \(T^2\). M Path length; path carries M + 1 marks. Validity holds M >= 1; larger M reduces Monte Carlo error. L Number kernel steps per path edge (.e. \(K^L\)). Larger L improves spread/mixing hence power. eps "mixture" (default) draws step size independently path edge fixed log-uniform eps_range. positive numeric value uses fixed step size, NULL uses 0.3. step size never tuned observed point, can break exactness. randomized TRUE (default) returns randomized upper-tail rank p-value, exactly \(\mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)\) \(H_0\); FALSE, ties broken conservatively. eps_range Bounds fixed log-uniform step-size mixture. cl_obs Optional precomputed cl_fun(X) (saves one call); otherwise computed internally. ridge Small non-negative ridge added pooled covariance computing reported observed \(T^2\) via hotelling_T2(). stiefel_tol Guard tolerance \(\max|Q'Q - |\) path (GUARD ). guard_feas_checks Number path points re-verify generic feasibility predicate (GUARD b). oracle_Sigma Optional known \(p \times p\) covariance matrix. supplied, additional known-\(\Sigma\) oracle p-value computed path ranking Mahalanobis statistic \(d' \Sigma^{-1} d\) pair-mean difference; returned p_oracle. Validity identical; statistic (hence power) differs. verbose TRUE, print one-block diagnostic. kernel Proposal Metropolis kernel. "givens" (default; random Givens kernel paper) picks two rows \(< j\) \(Q\) uniformly random proposes \(Q' = G_{ij}(\omega) Q\), rotation angle \(\omega \sim N(0, (\pi\,\mathrm{eps})^2)\) coordinate plane (see givens_left()). proposals symmetric preserve uniform law Stiefel manifold, kernels reversible w.r.t. \(\mathrm{Uniform}(E)\) p-value exact either; differ mixing, hence power. "cayley" proposes \(Q' = UQ\) \(U\) random Cayley rotation step eps, moves every row \(Q\) . eps, eps_range "mixture" rule apply . "givens_slice" shrinking-bracket Givens move (shrinkage step elliptical slice sampling; Neal 2003; Murray, Adams MacKay 2010): picks rows \(< j\) uniformly, draws \(\omega_0 \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 2\pi)\), sets bracket \([\omega_0 - 2\pi, \omega_0]\) (contains current point \(\omega = 0\)), proposes \(\omega = \omega_0\) , proposal infeasible, shrinks bracket toward 0 redraws \(\omega\) uniformly . reversible w.r.t. \(\mathrm{Uniform}(E)\), needs step size (eps eps_range ignored) nearly always moves, price several cl_fun calls per step (see n_path_calls). slice_max_props kernel = "givens_slice": maximum number proposals (calls cl_fun) one shrinking-bracket step; fail chain stays put. cap symmetric two directions move, kernel stays reversible p-value exact.

title: Algorithm-agnostic Besag-Clifford selective Hotelling test (arbitrary clustering) — selective_hotelling_bc
code: set.seed(1) X <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 2), 30, 2) # A deterministic, data-pure clustering routine (hierarchical clustering). hclust_cl <- function(Xmat) {   hc <- stats::hclust(stats::dist(Xmat), method = "average")   as.integer(stats::cutree(hc, k = 3)) } cl <- hclust_cl(X) # Pick a pair with at least 3 members each. sizes <- table(cl) big <- as.integer(names(sizes)[sizes >= 3]) res <- selective_hotelling_bc(X, hclust_cl, big[1], big[2], M = 60) res$pval #> [1] 0.6985158 print(res) #> Selective Hotelling T^2 test (unknown covariance) #>   Clusters tested : 2 vs 3 (of K = 3) #>   Sampler         : besag-clifford #>   Conditioning    : pair-preserved #>   Observed T^2    : 38.05 #>   Selective p-val : 0.6985 (MC s.e. ~ 0.059)
